why: Same notions. B reads Definition 2.7 existentially (f(O) ⊆ O' and f ∘ r sc-smooth for SOME r onto O); the project's IsScSmoothRetractMap quantifies over EVERY r, and isScSmoothRetractMap_iff_exists (Proposition 2.6 (1)) is exactly B's first conjunct for a retract O. With B's explicit TOB R identified with Tr(TU) (glue) and retractTangent_eq (Prop. 2.4, not an item theorem), B's independence of r, Tf(TO) ⊆ TO' and 'retractTangentMap = T(f∘r) on TO' are retractTangentMap_eqOn and tangentMap_mapsTo; B's fibrewise linearity (∃ L with T(f∘r)(o,h) = (f(o), Lh) ∈ T_{f(o)}O') follows with L = D(f∘r)(o). Conversely, since the project's predicate sees the target only through f(O) ⊆ O', B applied with the trivial target retract (E'₀, E'₀, E') (isScRetract_univ) gives the 'one r ⇒ every r' half and retractTangentMap_eqOn without assuming O' is a retract. Two conjuncts of A (continuousOn, mem_range_toBase: f is continuous and level-preserving on O) are not in the text's Definition 2.7 or in B; they were proved directly from the definitions.
